title: PERK: Long-Context Reasoning as Parameter-Efficient Test-Time Learning
claim: Learning is split into two nested loops: first encode context into a small adapter memory, then train it to reason.
layout: 2 panels, left-to-right, curved arrows linking inner and outer loops
description: Two dashed rounded panels sit side by side. The left one is titled 'Encoding the Context (Inner Loop Training)'. The right one is titled 'Learning to Reason (Outer Loop Training)'. Each panel has the same core block: a blue 'Pre-trained LLM' network icon with a snowflake (frozen), a plus sign, and an orange 'Memory Scratchpad' adapter icon with a flame (trainable). Under them are theta-base and theta-adaptors labels. On the left, stacked 'Relevant Documents K' (up to 8K tokens) feed in. On the right, a Question & Answer pair (Q:, A: bars) feeds in. A green loss pill (L_NLL on the left, L_reason on the right) sits at the end of each panel, with a gradient arrow looping back to the adapter parameters. Bold curved arrows between the panels show the nested cycle. The eye goes first to the blue and orange blocks.
caption: \textbf{Meta-learning \perk{} for long-context reasoning.} The training procedure involves a nested inner and outer loop. The inner loop optimizes the likelihood of a batch of long context segments with respect to the parameters of the LoRA-based memory scratchpad. In the outer loop, the model uses the encoded information in the memory scratchpad to answer questions. In both cases, only the memory scratchpad parameters are updated while the base LLM's parameters are frozen.
abstract: Long-context reasoning requires accurately identifying relevant information in extensive, noisy input contexts. In this work, we propose PERK (Parameter Efficient Reasoning over Knowledge), a scalable approach for learning to encode long contexts using gradient updates at test time. Specifically, PERK employs two nested optimization loops in a meta-training phase. The inner loop rapidly encodes contexts into a low-rank adapter (LoRA) that serves as a parameter-efficient memory module for the base model. Concurrently, the outer loop learns to use the updated adapter to accurately recall and reason over relevant information from the encoded long context. Our evaluations on several long-context reasoning tasks show that PERK significantly outperforms the standard long-context finetuning, achieving average absolute performance gains of up to 20% for Qwen-2.5 (0.5B & 7B) on synthetic and real-world long-context reasoning. PERK also maintains its advantages across model scales and families. Compared to specialized long-context LLMs, PERK matches or surpasses their performance. Finally, our analyses show PERK is more robust to reasoning complexity, length extrapolation, and the positions of relevant information in contexts.
